text:
The Panthers are 9-7-2 after losing in Washington on Saturday and in Boston on Sunday, two defeats in two days. For a team that won back-to-back Cups, that record looks alarming. Our numbers say it shouldn't, yet.

Florida takes 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and has finished 5.9 goals below its chances. By our count, it has about a point and a half fewer than its play deserves. The power play is excellent, producing 1.22 expected goals a game. The line of Sam Bennett and both Tkachuks has taken 59% of the expected goals together, and Brady Tkachuk, acquired from Ottawa in June, has been as advertised.

The problems are in net and in the lineup. Jacob Markstrom is at .874 over his last five starts, 3.7 goals worse than expected, and Florida needs saves more than it needs anything else. Anton Lundell just came back from a short injury absence. Yahoo reported Paul Maurice explaining why Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov are traveling on this road trip, and Marchand has spoken about a knee injury he feared could end his career. The Panthers also take almost six penalties a game, the kind of discipline problem that adds up.

Our playoff race gives them a 47% chance, projecting about 92 points. Watch Markstrom's next three starts.
headline: Florida's chances are fine. The goals aren't.
